summary.text:
Large, actively managed, and unusually well reconciled. Kent's balance sheet analysis holds on both of its own identities: a loans CFR of £1,276.2m is total debt of £826.8m plus internal borrowing of £449.4m, and balance sheet resources of £765.3m are that same £449.4m plus £315.9m of investments.

They spent the year taking debt off. £122.2m came out — £90m of it early repayment, including £50m of Barclays loans that delivered a discount to book cost and £40m of Dexia LOBOs the lender called. No new borrowing at all. Net debt costs finished £2.976m under budget. What remains is £610.3m at 4.2% over a value-weighted 21.9 years, with £50m of LOBOs still outstanding at 4.0%.

Two things are worth carrying forward. Dexia has now called at two councils in our reading — £40m here and £5m at Tameside — which is the kind of pattern only visible if you read everybody's papers. And Kent is deliberately shortening its investment portfolio, submitting redemption requests to the CCLA Property Fund because 'the return differential between these instruments and other liquid fixed income instruments has narrowed'. One officer address is published.

officer.subject: Dexia has called at two councils we've read this month
officer.body:
Hi Sangeeta,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts ahead of County Council on 17 September. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

Your balance sheet analysis at 4.1 is the cleanest presentation of internal borrowing we've come across. Both identities hold exactly — a loans CFR of £1,276.2m being total debt of £826.8m plus internal borrowing of £449.4m, and balance sheet resources of £765.3m being that same £449.4m plus the £315.9m of investments. Most reports make you do that arithmetic yourself, and plenty don't reconcile when you do.

The reason I'm writing is a pattern you're part of rather than anything about your position. Dexia exercised its option on your £40m LOBO during the year. It also called a £5m Tameside LOBO with a 16 June option date. Newcastle has had £27m called and repaid with another £81m still carrying options across this year and next, and Bath & North East Somerset's two KBC loans have run past their fixed period and now reset every six months. That's four councils in one month's reading, and the common thread is that rising rates have made these options worth exercising in a way they weren't for a decade.

You're ahead of it — £90m repaid early, including £50m of Barclays that delivered a discount to book cost, and net debt costs £2.976m under budget. But £50m of LOBOs is still outstanding at 4.0% over a value-weighted 37 years, and each option date is a decision taken against the market on the day rather than at the next report.

That's what pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis is for: every council's PWLB book priced each day against the DMO's repayment curve, so the premium or discount is a lookup. We never present it as a quote — the DMO's is the binding one — but it does mean the question of what a repayment costs is answerable on any given morning. Rates at both fixings are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard, and the monthly sector breakdown at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity: July was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers, average 5.02%.

One small thing on our side. Paragraph 6.3 gives the 10-year certainty rate at 5.73% and 20-year at 6.20% for 31 March; our own PM figures for that day are 5.72% and 6.23%. Within a couple of basis points, so almost certainly a different fixing rather than a disagreement — but I'd rather flag it than have you find it.

On training, three fit Kent: LOBO loans, for the £50m still running; Break costs and premature repayment, given what you executed this year; and our liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data and worth a look with CIPFA revising the Prudential and Treasury Codes. For members, Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) is written for exactly the scrutiny your Governance and Audit Committee gives this. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
